thread:
julia: Hey team — customer on Dedicated is seeing intermittent 429s even though they have a reserved pool. They say bursts start ~10s after a steady ramp.

sam: Which pool size and model are they on?

julia: Reserved pool: 4xA100, model: open-llama-13b, target concurrency ~60 req/s. They expected the pool to absorb bursts.

leo: 4 GPUs, 60 rps sounds high depending on token length. Any per-request token size?

julia: avg prompt 120 tokens, completion ~80 tokens. We measured p50 latency ~180ms when healthy.

maria: Can you paste the exact error payload from the client? 429 payloads have helpful headers.

julia: From customer logs: `{\"error\":\"rate_limited\", \"message\":\"quota exceeded\"}` and header dump: `x-rwrl-limit: 24000`, `x-rwrl-remaining: 0`, `x-rwrl-reset: 168`

sam: That looks like a token or unit quota burn, not the per-connection concurrency limiter. `x-rwrl-limit` shows allowed tokens for the window.

leo: Are they on a committed monthly token commit? If they are hitting token quota the pool will still accept requests but return 429 when the budget is exhausted.

julia: Customer says they have Reserved plan, but billing team confirms they've been on an annual reserved capacity contract; unclear if commit covers overage.

maria: Two orthogonal things to check: 1) serving-side throughput caps (per-pool TPS/capacity gating) and 2) account-level token budget. Both can produce 429s with similar client impact.

ops-bot: Deploy notice: router-v3.9 rolled out 03:20 UTC — no known regressions.

dan: Can we repro with a synthetic load targeted at the customer's pool? I can spin a load test from our staging account.

julia: yes please. customer provided the exact request pattern: 10s ramp to 60 rps, hold 45s, then idle 60s, repeat.

sam: Repro steps I used locally:
```
# simple curl loop (pseudo)
for i in {1..600}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
    -d '{\"model\":\"open-llama-13b\",\"input\":\"<payload>\",\"max_tokens\":80}' &
  sleep 0.016  # ~60 rps
done
```
Ran it against their pool and saw 429s after ~42s.

leo: Interesting — I instrumented router logs. We see a per-pool shaping rule kicking in: `throughput_cap_ms = 40000`, `burst_tokens = 24000`. When available tokens drop to zero, router starts returning 429.

maria: That config implies we maintain a token-bucket per-pool that is decoupled from GPU concurrency. The bucket drains with tokens consumed per output token.

julia: The customer thought the reserved GPUs would guarantee unlimited short bursts — need to update docs on this.

sam: Two immediate options for them: 1) increase burst allowance on their reserved pool, 2) increase committed token allowance or enable overage billing.

dan: Before changing billing, we should check latency SLOs if we relax shaping. If too many parallel in-flight requests, tail latency can blow up and we'd violate SLA.

leo: From the trace: peak queue depth increased from ~2 to ~18 when shaping disabled in a test — p95 jumped from 350ms to 1.2s. Not acceptable under their SLA.

maria: Suggest a phased approach: raise burst_tokens modestly (e.g., +50%) and enable a short-lived canary while monitoring p95. Also offer them an autoscale policy to spin an extra GPU for bursts.

julia: Customer also reported occasional 503 with `auth_failed` during the same windows. Could be token refresh/backoff causing retries.

sam: 503 auth_failed usually is 401/403 surface — can you grab a sample?

julia: snippet: `{\"error\":\"auth_failed\", \"reason\":\"billing_disabled\"}`. They had a billing hold triggered by suspicious usage alerts.

maria: That explains two layers: billing hold causes auth rejects (fail fast), then when billing resumed, they rapidly replayed queued requests causing token-bucket exhaustion -> 429.

dan: Repro note: If you simulate a billing pause and then resume with a replay of queued clients, the burst will exceed pool burst capacity even if GPUs are idle. So recommend client-side backoff on 429 and gradual ramp post-resume.

julia: Customer's SDK was configured to immediately retry 3x on any non-2xx without exponential backoff. We recommended switching to exponential jittered backoff (base 200ms, cap 5s).

leo: Add to triage checklist: confirm `x-rwrl-remaining` on 429, check billing status, check router shaping rules for the pool, check per-GPU queue depth and p95.

maria: I've drafted a recommended config snippet for them to add to their client app: 
```
retryPolicy: {
  maxAttempts: 5,
  backoff: {
    type: \"exponential_jitter\",
    base_ms: 200,
    max_ms: 5000
  },
  retryOn: [429, 503]
}
```
This will avoid stampedes after a billing resume.

julia: Customer asked whether we can map Reserved pool capacity to a higher per-pool token refill rate so bursts are absorbed without adding GPUs.

sam: We can, but it's a tradeoff. Increasing token refill increases burst absorb but raises risk of GPU saturation. We should tie any increase to an autoscaling policy that kicks an extra node when token burn rate exceeds X for Y seconds.

leo: Suggested autoscale rule: `if avg_token_burn_per_sec > pool_capacity * 0.8 for 30s then add 1 GPU` and `scale_down after 5m below 0.4`.

maria: I'll prepare a support playbook: root cause categories (billing hold -> replay, token quota -> 429, shaping -> config), immediate mitigations, and a recommended long-term solution (either increase commit or enable burst autoscale + client backoff).

julia: Customer accepted temporary burst increase + client SDK backoff. They're going to enable overage billing as a backup.

dan: Follow-up action items:
- leo: run a canary with +50% burst_tokens and monitor p95 for 30m (assigned).
- sam: coordinate with billing to confirm overage tolerance and update their account flags (assigned).
- maria: update the support KB with SDK backoff snippet and a short explanation of reserved pool token-bucket behavior (assigned).

ops-bot: Reminder: add postmortem if SLA blip > 5 minutes.

julia: Thanks all — I'll keep the thread updated with customer confirmation once they toggle overage. :thumbsup:

maria: FYI adding a short note to docs: "Reserved capacity guarantees raw GPU availability but not unlimited token budget; see token-bucket and burst config."

leo: done: created internal ticket INF-4723 to track pool burst tuning and autoscale templates.

julia: closing for now — will reopen if 429s persist after the canary.
